Kuss.et: From Middle High German kus, kos, from Old High German kus, kos, from Proto-West Germanic *koss. Compare Dutch kus, English kiss, Danish kys.

s: Sie küsste ihn nur wie eine Schwester.
She only kissed him like a sister.
Sie rannten hinaus in die Dunkelheit und küssten sich.
They ran off into the darkness and made out.
küssen.et: From Middle High German küssen, from Old High German kussen, from Proto-West Germanic *kussijan. Compare Dutch kussen, English kiss, Danish kysse.

Küste.et: From early modern Dutch kust(e) (“coast”), from Old French coste (“side; coast”), from Latin costa (“rib”). Compare modern French côte, English coast.

kuscheln.et: Iterative form of kuschen (“to lie down”) + -eln, from French se coucher. The form is late in standard usage (around 1900), but widespread and significantly older in dialects.

Küster.et: From Middle High German kuster, custer, from Old High German kustor, kostor, from Proto-West Germanic *kustārī.

s: Nur sieben Prozent der Erdoberfläche sind Küstengewässer.
Only seven percent of the earth's surface are coastal waters.

Kuschel.et:
* From Middle High German kuscheln (“to cuddle, snuggle”), from Old High German koschen.
* From Kusch + -el (diminutive suffix).
* Borrowed from Yiddish קושל (kushl), pet form of יקותיאל (yekusiel).
* Borrowed from Czech Kužel, from kužel (“distaff, cone”).

kusch.et: Originally hunting jargon, from French couche! (“lie down!”), from coucher. The use for “shoo” may or may not be the same word, see ksch for more.

s: to knuckle under, to kowtow (to act submissively)

Frohlocke nicht, wenn ich für diesmal kusche,
Wart nur, wart nur, bis ich dich einmal dusche!
»Bei denen heißt's noch immer, wenn unsereins den Mund auftut: Kusch dich! zu Hause — wie in der Bewegung,« sagte eine andere langjährige Parteigenossin.

Kustos.et: Borrowed from Latin custōs. Compare (obsolete) English custos (literally “warden”).

s: justice that is not hard enough
a town and rural district of Rhineland-Palatinate
inflated grade (high score regularly obtained at an educational institution with low effort)
Kuschelnote.et: From kuscheln (“cuddle; in compounds: cozy, = kuschelig”) + Note (“grade, mark”).

Kusch.et:
* Pet form of Old High German Godizo → Gozzo → Gutsch.
* Borrowed from Sorbian Kuš, pet form of the given name Markuš.
* Borrowed from Polish Kusz, Czech Kuš, or Hungarian Kus.
